GALLICA breaks the word across a line with NO hyphen -- the line ends 'Talium con', the next begins 'junctionem' -- so Migne's word is 'conjunctionem', entire, and the space is our transcription's. THE ARCHIVE at p.178 prints 'con-' / 'unctionem', having lost the j and supplied a hyphen: a well-formed jbig2 substitution that construes, and would have drawn a [sic:] from a stint working on the archive alone. No marker fired; TEI patch filed. Otherwise ZERO. Confirms Migne's readings behind three [var:] (Ex 20:4; Jn 14:9 'Qui enim videt Filium'; Ps 93:21 'Captabant ... condemnabant') and the UNCLOSED parenthesis at 0345B '(secundum illud: Qui devorant plebem meam ...'.
